chapter: First bands, illness and Houston life
title: Juneteenth in Texas and the Emancipation Day debate
summary: Cobb explains that Texas blacks celebrate Emancipation on the 19th of June, and the Danceses question how it relates to other dates.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Well, now when you recovered from the plurisy ...
Now wait a minute. Let me finish the situation with the drug store.
Okay.
And from the drug store, I'm still in music, now.
Yeah.
JAZZ FIELD
But I haven't gone in to the (unintelligible) or what have you, but I am trying to make a buck. And I didn't stay there but 8 months --that was as long as I stayed.

And when this other situation came up with the band, and I went downtown and I made a job -- we got a thing here in Houston, Texas the 19th of June, which is the Emancipation Day for blacks, in Texas.
Oh? Is that different from the national one?
Yeah.
Oh.
I told you about that.
Oh, did you really? I forget sometimes some of the things you tell me.
But that Emancipation Day is like the national later than the other, isn't it one -- when is the national one?
Well, you know what the national emancipation is --it's the Fourth of July!
The Fourth of July?
Yeah.
That's the date that the ...
But the black emancipation is the 19th of June, when Lincoln freed the slaves.
Right.
To save the union.
Is it the same as the rest of the country as in Texas?
Just Texas. As far as I know. Just Texas.
Yeah?

And that's a ritual. And they lost it for awhile and now they're bringing it back in. See, last year we had a situation at Miller Theatre here with Johnny [Hoop,] Eddie Clean head VINSON Benson -- or just a blues festival relating to blacks and their heritage, for a whole day, evening and a matinee and at night --and it's coming back again this year. That was the first establishment of it.

And then on the 19th of June here now, the NAACP sponsors a parade in the Miller middle of the Theatre, with this city of Houston and the Musicians' and Performers' Trust Fund pay for the musicians to play for this. The 19th of June.
Yeah, I know, but the two Americans, you're kind of kidding me about this, but ...
Now what do you mean, 'kidding' you?
What I'm trying to find out is that you see, slavery was abolished in the British Empire about 1934. Now when you abolished it ...
1834! I beg your pardon. 1834.
Now, the thing I don't understand, frankly, is are you telling
me that the emancipation of the slaves was celebrated nationally on the 19th of June?
I didn't say that.
Only in Texas?
Texas recognizes it as the 19th of June.
Well, does that give up the date ...
I'm giving you black history here.
But I mean, the date is the when Lincoln freed the slaves the 19th of June?
When he freed the slaves to save the union?
Yeah ... well, what was the date on that?
I don't have the date on it.
But the 19th ...
The only thing I can say to you is that the date that they picked in Texas was the 19th of June. Now why, I don't know on that.
Well, I meant ...
